## Objective
- Build a complete, playable offline mobile tactical FPS inspired by Counter-Strike 2.

## Requirements
- Build now without clarification; make reasonable assumptions.
- Support mobile play and offline use; check the game in screenshots saved as small JPEGs.

## Decisions
- Created an original single-player game called DUSTLINE rather than reproducing Counter-Strike 2 assets or branding.
- Implemented a self-contained raycast FPS with procedural graphics and no external gameplay assets; added a service worker for offline caching.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built a playable 5-hostile mission with movement, aiming, shooting, reloads, enemy attacks, health/armor, minimap, win/loss screens, and restart.
- Added desktop keyboard/mouse controls and mobile joystick, touch-look, and fire/reload controls.
- Added PWA manifest, icon, and offline service worker.
- Started the local server and checked desktop and phone-sized views; confirmed firing can neutralize an enemy.

### Active
- Final verification and any polish still needed.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest `screenshots/latest.jpg` if visual verification is needed.
2. Run a fuller gameplay check, including reload, enemy damage, and win/loss completion.
3. Check `git status` and report the changes as uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and PWA registration.
- `game.js`: Raycast rendering, gameplay, bots, controls, HUD, and match flow.
- `style.css`: Desktop/mobile styling.
- `sw.js`: Offline asset caching.
- `manifest.webmanifest`: Installable app metadata.
- `icon.svg`: App icon.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Most recent visual check.

## Important Context
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- A Playwright test started the match and fired once; the HUD showed `1 / 5` hostiles neutralized.
- The browser initially reported a missing `/favicon.ico`; an SVG favicon was subsequently added.

## Findings

- **Real dual-touch conflict — releasing the look finger can stop held fire.** On mobile, a touch that starts on the canvas is handled by the touch-look listeners, but it also generates pointer events. If one finger is holding the fire button (`mouseDown = true`) and a second finger looks on the canvas, that second finger’s `pointerup` reaches the canvas handler and unconditionally sets `mouseDown = false`. Sustained fire therefore stops when the look finger is lifted, even while the fire finger remains down. See [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js:21`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js ) and [line 23]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js ).

  **Minimal fix:** Scope the canvas `pointerup` reset to a mouse pointer that began firing on the canvas; the fire button already resets its own state on `pointerup` and `pointercancel`. For more robust handling, track the active fire pointer/source rather than sharing an unqualified boolean.

- **Look state is not cleared on touch cancellation.** `lookTouch` is cleared on `touchend`, but there is no `touchcancel` handler. A canceled touch can leave stale look state until another qualifying touch replaces it. This is a smaller robustness issue than the firing conflict. See [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js:22`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js ).

  **Minimal fix:** Clear the matching `lookTouch` on `touchcancel`, just as on `touchend`.

## Otherwise

- The joystick uses its own pointer ID and pointer capture, so its movement and release handling are separated from canvas touch-look. The fire button also has its own pointer release/cancel handlers.
- On a typical narrow mobile-emulation viewport, the look listener can receive canvas touches while joystick and fire touches target their overlaid controls; the code’s touch-look threshold also ignores starts in the leftmost 42% of the screen.
- HUD overlays can intercept touches because they sit above the canvas, so a look drag started over those regions will not reach the canvas listener. That appears to be a coverage limitation rather than an event conflict.

This is a static code review; I did not run browser emulation.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build DUSTLINE into an offline mobile tactical FPS with a bomb-planting mode.
- Add tactical/butterfly/karambit/bayonet knives, weapons, skins, operators, cases, and 3D presentation.

## Requirements
- Make reasonable assumptions without clarification.
- Check gameplay in small JPEG screenshots.
- Provide exactly one mode: bomb planting.

## Decisions
- DUSTLINE is an original single-player game using procedural graphics and no external gameplay assets.
- The existing game uses a 2D raycast renderer; the requested 3D presentation remains to be implemented.

## Work State
### Completed
- Base playable FPS implemented: movement, aiming, shooting, reloading, hostile AI, health/armor, minimap, win/loss screens, restart, and desktop/mobile controls.
- PWA manifest, SVG icon, and offline service worker added.
- Earlier checks verified `node --check game.js`, basic firing/reloading, service worker/manifest, and desktop/phone-sized views; screenshot at `screenshots/latest.jpg`.

### Active
- Bomb-mode interface edits started, but planting, defending, detonation, and bomb timers are not implemented.
- Loadout selectors and case UI added; persistence, case opening/rewards, and gameplay integration are incomplete.
- Knife selection/toggle and procedural first-person knife drawing started; knife melee and weapon/loadout behavior need validation and completion.
- Requested 3D rendering, weapons, operators, and skins remain incomplete; current rendering is not true 3D.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect and complete `game.js` and `index.html`; implement one functional bomb-plant/defend mode and verify its win/loss flow.
2. Finish and test knife melee, weapon options, operator/skin selection, and case opening/reward persistence; fix any markup or runtime issues.
3. Decide and implement a feasible 3D approach, then test desktop/mobile gameplay and save updated JPEG screenshots.
4. Check the existing listener on port 3000 before attempting a server restart; the previous `./start.sh` attempt failed with `EADDRINUSE`.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, mission overlays, loadout selectors, case controls, and mobile controls.
- `game.js`: Gameplay, rendering, enemy AI, weapons, knives, and current partial feature implementations.
- `style.css`: Desktop/mobile layout and UI styling.
- `sw.js`: Offline asset caching.
- `manifest.webmanifest`: Installable app metadata.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Earlier visual check.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The bomb-site coordinates and several bomb-mode variables are present in `game.js`, but gameplay logic is unfinished.
- Case and loadout UI elements have been added without complete behavior or verification.

## Objective
- Build DUSTLINE into an offline mobile tactical FPS with a functional bomb-planting mode and expanded loadout and presentation features.

## Requirements
- Provide exactly one mode: bomb planting.
- Include tactical, butterfly, karambit, and bayonet knives.
- Check gameplay in small JPEG screenshots.

## Decisions
- DUSTLINE is an original single-player game using procedural graphics and no external gameplay assets.
- The existing renderer is 2D raycasting; true 3D presentation remains outstanding.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added bomb planting and detonation timers, objective HUD, loadout selectors, case controls, persistence, weapon-specific capacities, and knife melee logic.
- Confirmed `node --check game.js` passes and the existing server on port 3000 responds with HTTP 200.

### Active
- Test gameplay and browser runtime, including planting/detonation, loadout persistence and rewards, mobile controls, and save updated JPEG screenshots.
- Review bomb-mode outcome logic and complete the plant-and-defend gameplay.
- Implement a feasible true-3D presentation approach.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Open the running app at `http://localhost:3000` with Playwright; inspect the console and capture desktop and phone-sized JPEG screenshots.
2. Test the plant-and-defend flow, weapon reload capacities, case persistence/rewards, loadout selection, and knife melee; fix any issues.
3. Review whether enemies should defuse or otherwise contest the planted bomb.
4. Address the outstanding true-3D presentation goal.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Gameplay, rendering, AI, bomb-mode logic, loadout, cases, and knife behavior.
- `index.html`: HUD, bomb-mode interface, selectors, case controls, and mobile controls.
- `style.css`: Game layout, responsive styling, and bomb/loadout UI.
- `sw.js`: Offline asset caching.
- `screenshots/`: Existing screenshots; save updated JPEG checks here.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Bomb planting requires holding E or the mobile plant control near Site A for three seconds; detonation follows after 35 seconds.
- Enemy defusal behavior remains unimplemented or unverified.
- The renderer remains 2D raycasting, not true 3D.
- Do not restart the server: port 3000 is already occupied by the app and returns HTTP 200.
